ratio, active  past ratio, committed future ratio, sentence-level lexical repetitiveness, hedging term  density, and text complexity as measured by the gunning fog index. group differences were  evaluated using permutation tests, measuring the differences in medians. for the false  discovery rate correction, the benjamini-hochberg correction was applied separately within  each hypothesis family.  before correction, four comparisons reached conventional significance: passive voice use in  both regional comparisons, active past use among b corp certified companies, and  readability among us-based companies, with the regional comparisons producing large  effect sizes. after fdr correction, two findings were retained: passive voice use and active  past use, both among certified companies comparing eu and us groups. these patterns  suggest that regional reporting culture, potentially shaped by differences in regulatory  context between the eu and the us, accounts for the most pronounced stylometric variation  in this sample, rather than certification status.  no statistically significant stylometric differences were detected between b corp-certified  and non-certified companies after correction, suggesting that certification may shape the  content of sustainability disclosures without systematically altering their linguistic form.  overall, the results caution against treating individual stylometric markers as standalone  indicators of greenwashing risk. they may, however, serve as useful contextual signals when  combined with claim-level verification or quantitative esg data.
key_words: stylometry; sustainability reporting; stylometric features; natural language processing; nlp; corporate sustainability reporting; communication; environment; b corporation; b  corps

title: Efektivnost finančních trhů: empirická analýza indexu DXY a rozvíjejících se trhů
author: sidenko rostislav
title_eng: testing market efficiency: evidence from the us dollar index and emerging markets
abstract: his bachelor thesis investigates whether financial markets contain exploitable predictive structure or are efficient in the weak and semi-strong forms of the efficient market hypothesis (emh). the analysis focuses on two liquid instruments that represent different segments of the global financial system: the u.s. dollar index (dxy), as a proxy for a mature developed market, and the ishares msci emerging markets etf (eem), as a benchmark for emerging equity markets. the thesis develops a forecasting framework that combines traditional time-series econometrics with modern machine learning techniques to assess the predictability of returns relative to a simple benchmark model, and to systematically model the conditional volatility. by comparing results across dxy and eem, the study examines how market maturity and institutional quality shape the limits of predictability, and whether advanced predictive algorithms translate into economically meaningful gains for active trading strategies.
key_words: machine learning,; efficient market hypothesis,; emerging markets; time series forecasting,; us dollar index; predictive modelling; volatility modelling

title: Geolokace textu na základě pojmenovaných entit a znalostních bází
author: palyzová adéla
title_eng: text geolocation based on named entities and knowledge bases
abstract: this thesis examines how geolocation systems perform on indirect locational reference - texts where location must be inferred without explicit place names, where toponyms are ambiguous, or where entity names are shared across multiple real-world referents in different places. these cases represent a documented failure boundary for standard geoparsing but have not been evaluated under controlled conditions in existing benchmarks. a synthetic dataset of 360 entries is constructed around three signal types: indirect entity inference (no toponym present), ambiguous toponyms, and ambiguous entity names. seven pipeline architectures drawn from three paradigms - two-stage entity linking, end-to-end entity linking, and prompt-engineered large language models - are evaluated against this benchmark across clean and noisy conditions, two text formats, and six continents. the findings show that no single paradigm dominates across all three signal types. entity linking handles ambiguous toponyms most reliably; large language models handle indirect inference better due to their parametric world knowledge; ambiguous entity names remain hard for all systems. a routing architecture that selects between entity linking and an llm per text achieves the most consistent performance on clean data but proves fragile under noise. geographic bias toward europe and north america is present in every pipeline tested. results are validated against geocorpora real tweets, confirming the paradigm patterns transfer beyond synthetic data. the thesis contributes a reusable benchmark isolating signal types that aggregate evaluations obscure and demonstrates that combining existing paradigms is more effective than any single one - while arguing that the field should work toward unified models capable of handling both indirect inference and toponym disambiguation natively.
key_words: geolocation from text; natural language processing; indirect locational reference; toponym disambiguation; geoparsing; named entity recognition; wikidata; geographic information systems; entity linking; large language models

title: Time series analysis and short-term prediction of particle pollution in Central Europe (1990-2022)
author: hujerová lucie
title_eng: time series analysis and short-term prediction of particle pollution in central europe (1990-2022)
abstract: this bachelor thesis focuses on the time series analysis of particle pollution data in central europe, specifically czechia, slovakia, poland, germany, austria and switzerland, between 1990 and 2022. furthermore, trend modelling is applied to generate a five-year forecast. the main objective of the analysis is to explore patterns in pm emissions in central europe over time and to compare these findings across the countries studied. additionally, countries are classified into two larger groups: west-central european countries (germany, austria and switzerland) and east-central european countries (czechia, slovakia and poland); to compare underlying similarities and differences within and between these groups, which might be interlinked with the groups’ different economic and historical background.
key_words: time series; time series analysis; forecasting; fine particle pollution; coarse particle pollution; central europe; trend

title: Přechod na postkvantovou kryptografii v podnikovém prostředí
author: kresl filip
title_eng: transitioning to post-quantum cryptography in business
abstract: this thesis analyzes the practical migration of enterprise web infrastructure to nist-standardized post-quantum cryptography to mitigate the immediate threat of store now, decrypt later attacks. following a review of standardized migration frameworks, a technical case study was executed to upgrade a containerized tls 1.2 environment to a quantum-resistant tls 1.3 stack. the implementation replaced vulnerable components by enforcing a hybrid x25519 and ml-kem-768 key exchange, deploying ml-dsa-65 for server authentication, and utilizing aes-256 for symmetric encryption. network traffic analysis showed that the 5,515-byte ml-dsa certificate exceeds standard mtu limits and causes tcp fragmentation, marking increased payload size as the primary operational challenge. however, isolating the cryptographic overhead, the comparison between classical and post-quantum tls 1.3 handshakes showed an increase in connection setup time of only 4 ms (from 142 ms to 146 ms) under simulated network latency. the migration to lattice-based cryptography is therefore technically viable for current infrastructures, provided that the increased bandwidth consumption is properly managed.
key_words: post-quantum cryptography; pqc; transport layer security; tls; hybrid cryptography; ml-kem; ml-dsa

title: Využití PTP v sítích AVoIP
author: olszynský richard
title_eng: use of ptp in avoip networks
abstract: this bachelor’s thesis focuses on the design, implementation, and evaluation of a low-cost, gnss-synchronized ptp grandmaster for avoip networks. modern avoip protocols, such as dante and aes67, require strict time synchronization to ensure precise media playback without audio dropouts or artifacts. while commercial grandmaster clocks are available, this thesis explores a custom solution based on consumer-grade hardware, specifically raspberry pi 5 and adafruit ultimate gps hat.  the theoretical part introduces the core principles of time synchronization in networked systems, compares ntp and ptp protocols, details the ieee 1588 standard, and explores avoip timing requirements.  the practical part describes the hardware assembly and software configuration of the grandmaster clock. the system utilizes a 1pps hardware interrupt, nmea time data, and a set of linux packages that include gpsd, chrony, phc2sys, and ptp4l. to improve synchronization precision, two software optimizations were implemented: cpu core isolation and nic interrupt coalescing.  the resulting grandmaster was deployed and tested within a dante-enabled university network. the evaluation showed that cpu core isolation successfully reduced the standard deviation of hardware clock offset by more than three times (from 388.8 to 117.4 ns). further testing demonstrated robust system stability during simulated network, gps, and power outages, showcasing its viability in a production avoip environment.
key_words: precision time protocol; ptp; audio over ip; avoip; grandmaster; gps; ieee 1588; dante; aes67; raspberry pi

title: Návrh vizuální identity pro e-shop s čajem
author: mulyukova adelina
title_eng: visual identity design for a tea e-shop
abstract: this bachelor's thesis documents the design of a visual identity for a fictional sustainable premium specialty tea e-commerce brand. the work combines a theoretical foundation in visual branding with a practical design process grounded in market analysis, competitive analysis, target audience research, and qualitative evaluation. the theoretical part defines the relationships between branding, brand identity, and visual identity, and examines how core visual elements (logo design, colour palette, and typography) shape consumer perception, build emotional connection, and influence purchasing decisions. it also addresses the strategic foundations of brand identity development: mission, vision, values, positioning, brand archetypes, and target audience expectations. the practical part applies this framework to the development of a complete visual identity system. analysis of the specialty tea e-commerce market identified premiumisation, sustainability, and ritual consumption as the primary growth drivers. structured visual analysis of five competing brands revealed a market dominated by green colour palettes, botanical illustration, and heritage ornamentation, with no brand building its identity around the sensory experience of drinking tea itself. this gap informed the positioning and visual direction of the proposed brand. the resulting brand, initially named chaté and subsequently, following qualitative evaluation, revised to chaya, is built around the concept of tea as a reason to slow down. the visual system consists of a deep warm brown-black and off-white cream colour palette, a wordmark set in cormorant garamond, a brush stroke as the sole recurring graphic element, and a cylindrical wooden tube as the primary packaging format. the identity was evaluated through six semi-structured interviews with members of the target audience. findings confirmed strong performance on attractiveness and credibility, with targeted revisions made in response to feedback on label clarity, cultural ambiguity in the brand name, product photography range, and body typeface pairing. the thesis demonstrates that a research-informed design process can produce a visual identity that is both strategically differentiated and positively received by the intended audience.
key_words: tea e-commerce; sustainable branding; brand archetypes; packaging design; brand identity; visual identity; brand positioning

title: VST3 Plugin pro úpravu sub-basových frekvencí na základě vnímané hlasitosti lidským uchem
author: pavelka ondřej
title_eng: vst3 plugin for attenuating sub-bass frequencies based on perceived loudness of human ear
abstract: this bachelor’s thesis addresses one of the most persistent challenges in modern audio production, the accurate management and reproduction of the sub-bass region (20 hz to 60-80 hz). due to the non-linearity of the human auditory system which is described by the normal equal-loudness-level contours (iso 226:2023), humans are significantly less sensitive to these low frequencies than to the midrange, leading to a critical disparity between measured loudness and subjectively perceived loudness.  the theoretical part of this work examines the human auditory system and the specific characteristics of the sub-bass region, investigating psychoacoustic phenomena, such as the ”missing fundamental”, that govern how humans interpret low-end frequencies. the research evaluates existing static and dynamic mixing workflows, including combination of these workflows, reinforcing that even these standard methodologies are effective for maintaining consistent perceived loudness across the sub-bass spectrum when rightly calibrated to human hearing sensitivities.  the practical outcome of this thesis is the design and implementation of a vst3 plugin developed using the juce framework and c++, that can run on all major operating systems and daws. the plugin utilizes a two-stage signal chain, a static equalization stage based on equal-loudness curves and a frequency-aware saturation stage to generate harmonic overtones. qualitative feedback from musicians and audio engineers confirms that the tool can provide a perceptually accurate results, but that there are still a lot of variables the plugin can not control. despite these challenges, initial feedback suggests the plugin represents a step in the right direction for addressing the gap between objective signal intensity and human hearing sensitivity and that the plugins potential use can go beyond equalizing sub-bass frequencies. performance testing indicates a higher computational demand than standard stock plugins, identifying a key area for future optimization.
key_words: lufs; eq; compression; juce; dbfs; sub-bass; vst3

title: Predikce výhry profesionálních zápasů v Dota 2
author: koberec matěj
title_eng: win prediction for professional matches in dota 2
abstract: this thesis is dedicated to the subject matter of win prediction in an esport title dota 2. the aim of the thesis is construction of models for prediction with the use of data, which are available before the beginning of the match in the shape of selected heroes and data obtained through the progression of a match at the 10 minute mark, such as difference in gold between teams, difference in taken towers or amount of activated runes. there is description of data in the thesis, the construction of logistic regression, random forest and extreme gradient boosting models. the logistic regression model is constructed with all variables except the difference in gold and experience, which have high multicollinearity with the other variables, but are kept in the random forest and extreme gradient boosting models to capture more complex relationships between variables. all the created models are then evaluated with the use of evaluation metrics and their quality of prediction is compared between them.
key_words: win prediction; dota 2; logistic regression; machine learning models
